high.title: S&P Global Ratings Affirms Indonesia Credit Rating at BBB/A-2 with Stable Outlook
high.summary: S&P Global Ratings has reaffirmed Indonesia's sovereign credit rating at BBB (long-term) and A-2 (short-term) with a stable outlook, keeping the country firmly in investment-grade territory. The rating is supported by strong economic growth prospects, prudent macroeconomic policy, and relatively low external and government debt. Coordinating Minister Airlangga Hartarto highlighted this as a positive signal for investors that Indonesia's economic fundamentals remain solid amid rising global uncertainty.

high.title: S&P Projects Rupiah to Strengthen to Rp 17,700/USD; Current Rate at Rp 18,109
high.summary: S&P Global Ratings projects the Indonesian rupiah will strengthen to Rp 17,700 per US dollar in 2026 and further to Rp 17,500 in 2027, suggesting meaningful upside from the current level. As of Monday's close, the rupiah was trading weaker at Rp 18,109/USD, down 0.24%. This projection, tied to Indonesia's affirmed investment-grade rating, is significant for currency traders and businesses with USD-denominated obligations.

high.title: President Prabowo Approves Special Fuel Price of Rp 15,000/Liter for Fishing Vessels
high.summary: President Prabowo Subianto has approved a special subsidized diesel fuel price of Rp 15,000 per liter for fishing vessel operators with boat sizes between 30 and 200 gross tons, well below the recent non-subsidized market price of Rp 21,300/liter. The government set this price based on an estimated average domestic diesel production cost of Rp 18,600/liter, representing a significant subsidy for the fisheries sector. This policy decision has implications for state energy company finances, the fisheries industry, and government subsidy expenditure.

high.title: IHSG Surges Strongly, Returns to 6,000 Level
high.summary: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) closed up 1.92% at 6,037.84 on Monday, July 13, recovering from an opening level of 5,934.71. Trading volume reached 26.30 billion shares with a transaction value of Rp 12.13 trillion. The return to the 6,000 level marks a significant short-term recovery for the Indonesian stock market.

high.title: S&P Rating Announcement Seen as Fresh Boost for IHSG
high.summary: S&P Global Ratings maintained Indonesia's sovereign debt rating at BBB (long-term) and A-2 (short-term) with a stable outlook, which analysts at MNC Sekuritas credit as a key driver of the IHSG's 1.92% rally to 6,037.84. The decision signals continued international confidence in Indonesia's fiscal stability and creditworthiness. This rating affirmation is expected to support short-term investor confidence in Indonesian capital markets.

high.title: Revealed: The Root Cause Behind the US Dollar Briefly Pushing Rupiah to Rp 18,000
high.summary: The Indonesian Rupiah briefly touched Rp 18,000 per US Dollar near the close of trading on July 6, 2026, driven by hawkish signals from Federal Reserve officials pushing the DXY dollar index to a one-year high. Bank Indonesia confirmed that the Fed held its federal funds rate at 3.50%–3.75% in June but markets are now pricing in potential rate hikes ahead. The renewed dollar strength poses ongoing pressure on the Rupiah and Indonesian capital flows.

high.title: Trump Declares US 'Guardian of the Strait of Hormuz,' Imposes 20% Tariff on All Cargo
high.summary: President Trump announced that the US will act as 'Guardian of the Strait of Hormuz' and impose a 20% fee on all cargo transiting the strategically vital waterway, amid the ongoing US-Israel-Iran conflict. This move carries significant implications for global shipping costs and energy supply chains, particularly for Indonesia as a major importer of oil and goods transiting through the strait. Legal and implementation questions remain unresolved, adding uncertainty to global commodity and energy markets.

high.title: Trump Claims US is Guardian of Strait of Hormuz, to Impose 20% Tariff on Cargo
high.summary: US President Donald Trump announced a 20% tariff on all cargo passing through the Strait of Hormuz, declaring the US as the official guardian of the strategic waterway. This move has significant implications for global energy and shipping costs, as the Strait of Hormuz is a critical chokepoint for oil and gas exports from the Middle East. Indonesian businesses and investors should monitor potential increases in energy import costs and supply chain disruptions that could ripple into domestic inflation.

high.title: Root Cause of Still-High Rice Prices Revealed
high.summary: Indonesia's National Food Agency (Bapanas) revealed that persistently high rice prices are driven by elevated prices of dry unhusked rice (GKP) at the farmer level, currently at Rp 7,000–7,500/kg, well above the Rp 6,500/kg assumption used to set the Maximum Retail Price (HET). This structural mismatch makes it virtually impossible to bring retail rice prices down to government-mandated levels. Continued rice price pressure poses a significant risk to headline inflation and household purchasing power in Indonesia.

high.title: Trump Declares US as 'Guardian of the Strait of Hormuz', Imposes 20% Levy on All Cargo Passing Through
high.summary: President Trump announced the US will act as 'Guardian of the Strait of Hormuz' and charge a 20% fee on all cargo transiting the strategically vital waterway amid ongoing US-Israel-Iran conflict. This move has significant implications for global shipping costs and oil supply chains, as the Strait of Hormuz is a critical passage for a large portion of the world's oil exports. Indonesian businesses and commodity exporters/importers could face higher freight and energy costs if the policy is implemented.

high.title: Indonesian Capital Market Investors Now Surpass 30 Million
high.summary: OJK Chairwoman Friderica Widyasari Dewi announced that Indonesia's capital market investors have surpassed 30 million people, up from 20 million in 2025 — a remarkable addition of 10 million investors in just half a year. This milestone signals strong retail participation growth, which OJK views as a key buffer for financial market stability. The surge in retail investors reduces market vulnerability to foreign capital outflows and strengthens domestic market resilience.

high.title: IDX Demutualization Regulation Targeted for September; BI and Danantara to Hold Exchange Shares
high.summary: OJK is targeting the completion of its regulatory framework (POJK) for the demutualization of the Indonesia Stock Exchange (BEI) by September 2026, following discussions with Coordinating Minister for the Economy Airlangga Hartarto. Under the P2SK Law, the Ministry of Finance, Bank Indonesia, and BPI Danantara are among entities eligible to hold shares in the exchange post-demutualization. This is a landmark structural reform for Indonesia's capital markets, opening BEI ownership to government institutions and potentially the public.

medium.title: Indonesian Ministry of Finance Responds to S&P Rating Affirmation: International Community Still Trusts Indonesia
medium.summary: Indonesia's Ministry of Finance welcomed S&P's decision to maintain Indonesia's BBB/A-2 credit rating, citing it as evidence of sustained international confidence in the country's fiscal discipline and economic resilience. Director General Herman Saheruddin emphasized that Indonesia has maintained consistent fiscal discipline in line with directives from President Prabowo and the Finance Minister. The government also pointed to Indonesia's robust economic growth engines as key factors underpinning confidence amid global turbulence.

medium.title: Microsoft Lays Off 4,800 Employees (2.1% of Workforce) to Cut Costs in AI Era; Xbox Division Hardest Hit
medium.summary: Microsoft is laying off approximately 4,800 employees, representing 2.1% of its global workforce, as part of a cost-cutting strategy aligned with its pivot toward artificial intelligence. The Xbox division is the most severely impacted, losing around one-fifth of its staff, including 1,600 roles cut on July 6 with more reductions planned. This move reflects broader global tech sector restructuring trends that may influence Indonesian tech industry sentiment and Microsoft's local operations.

medium.title: New OJK Rule on Pension Funds: Pension Benefits Can Now Be Paid in Lump Sum
medium.summary: Indonesia's Financial Services Authority (OJK) issued Decision KEP-54/D.05/2026, allowing pension benefit payments — including severance pay, service awards, and rights compensation — to be made in a lump sum, following two Constitutional Court rulings (No. 139/PUU-XXIII/2025 and No. 164/PUU-XXIII/2025). The regulation aims to provide legal certainty for pension fund participants, surviving spouses, and children while maintaining industry stability. The rule remains in effect until superseded by new legislation.

medium.title: IDX on Buzz Linking IHSG Movements to President Prabowo's Speech
medium.summary: Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) President Director Jeffrey Hendrik pushed back on viral social media claims linking IHSG movements directly to President Prabowo Subianto's speeches, stating that the correlation between politics and investment decisions has significantly weakened compared to the 1980s. He emphasized that modern market dynamics are driven more by economic fundamentals than political events. The statement is intended to reassure investors and reduce market speculation tied to political sentiment.

medium.title: IDX Opens Door for BYD and Tencent to Enter Indonesian Capital Market via Single Stock Futures
medium.summary: The Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) is finalizing an agreement with Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing (HKEx) to allow major Chinese companies such as BYD and Tencent to be listed on the Indonesian market through Single Stock Futures (SSF) instruments. This dual-listing mechanism would expand investment options for Indonesian investors and increase the attractiveness and competitiveness of the local capital market. The initiative signals a broader effort by IDX to internationalize its product offerings and attract foreign interest.

medium.title: OJK Chief Reveals Key Reasons Why Online Gambling is So Difficult to Eradicate in Indonesia
medium.summary: OJK Chairwoman Friderica Widyasari Dewi identified six major challenges in combating online gambling in Indonesia, highlighting that it has evolved into a sophisticated, cross-border organized crime ecosystem exploiting digital manipulation and technology. The financial regulator's acknowledgment underscores systemic risks to Indonesia's banking and payment systems, as illicit fund flows through the financial sector remain difficult to detect and block. This has direct regulatory implications for Indonesian banks and fintech companies required to strengthen anti-money laundering compliance.

medium.title: Online Gambling Syndicates Pay Farmers and Housewives Rp 100,000–500,000 to Open Bank Accounts
medium.summary: Indonesia's Minister of Communication and Digital Affairs revealed that online gambling operators are exploiting vulnerable low-income individuals, including farmers and housewives, by paying them Rp 100,000–500,000 to open bank accounts used as conduits for illegal financial transactions. The government is urging banks to strengthen Know Your Customer (KYC) procedures, especially in remote areas, to detect and prevent account misuse before it occurs. This highlights growing pressure on Indonesian financial institutions to enhance compliance frameworks and anti-money laundering controls.

medium.title: Finance Minister Responds to ICW Findings of Budget Markup in Village Cooperative Pickup Truck Procurement
medium.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa responded to allegations by Indonesian Corruption Watch (ICW) of budget inflation in the procurement of pickup trucks for the government's Village Cooperative (Kopdes Merah Putih) program, stating that disbursements will only be made after a formal audit process. ICW has indicated it will report the alleged irregularities to the Corruption Eradication Commission (KPK), raising governance concerns around a key government economic program. Investors and observers should monitor this case as it may affect sentiment around government spending credibility and the broader rural economic development agenda.

medium.title: National Economic Council Meets President Prabowo at Hambalang Residence
medium.summary: The National Economic Council (DEN), led by Chairman Luhut Binsar Pandjaitan and including prominent economists such as Chatib Basri and Mari Elka Pangestu, briefed President Prabowo Subianto on the latest national economic developments and submitted strategic recommendations. The council also reported progress on the GovTech digital government transformation initiative aimed at improving data accuracy and ensuring targeted distribution of government programs. This meeting signals active high-level coordination on economic strategy and digital governance, which could influence upcoming policy directions.

medium.title: Chicken and Egg Prices at Farm Level Begin to Recover — Here's Why
medium.summary: Bapanas reported that chicken and egg prices at the farm level are gradually recovering, driven by the resumption of the Free Nutritious Meals (MBG) school program and the end of the Javanese month of Suro, which traditionally suppresses demand for celebratory events. The temporary halt of MBG during school holidays had previously weighed on poultry demand and prices. The recovery in these key food commodity prices is relevant for inflation monitoring and the performance of the Indonesian poultry sector.

medium.title: Trump Family Earns Rp 5.39 Trillion from Middle East Business Dealings
medium.summary: US President Donald Trump and his family reportedly earned approximately US$300 million (Rp 5.39 trillion) from Middle East business activities in 2025, primarily from the sale of a stake in crypto firm World Liberty Financial to a UAE royal family-linked entity, alongside property development deals. This raises concerns about potential conflicts of interest influencing US foreign and trade policy in the Middle East region. For Indonesian investors, this context is relevant when assessing the geopolitical motivations behind US policy moves such as the Strait of Hormuz tariff announcement.

medium.title: OJK Chief Reveals Why Online Gambling is So Hard to Eradicate in Indonesia
medium.summary: OJK Chairwoman Friderica Widyasari Dewi identified six major challenges in combating online gambling in Indonesia, citing rapid domain-switching, cross-border organized crime, and the manipulation of digital spaces as key obstacles. The regulator's acknowledgment highlights ongoing systemic risks within Indonesia's financial and digital ecosystem. This is relevant for banking sector investors as it signals continued regulatory pressure on financial institutions to strengthen monitoring and compliance.

medium.title: Online Gambling Syndicates Pay Farmers and Housewives Rp 100,000–500,000 to Open Bank Accounts
medium.summary: Indonesia's Minister of Communication and Digital Affairs revealed that online gambling syndicates are exploiting low-income individuals, including farmers and housewives, by paying them Rp 100,000–500,000 to open bank accounts used as illegal transaction conduits. The government is calling on banks to strengthen their Know Your Customer (KYC) processes, especially in rural areas, to prevent such misuse. This signals upcoming regulatory scrutiny and potential compliance cost increases for Indonesian banks.

medium.title: Finance Minister Responds to Allegations of Budget Mark-Up in Village Cooperative Pickup Truck Procurement
medium.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa responded to Indonesian Corruption Watch (ICW) findings alleging budget inflation in the procurement of pickup trucks for the Kopdes Merah Putih cooperative program, stating that disbursements will only be made after a formal audit. ICW has announced plans to report the alleged corruption to the KPK (Corruption Eradication Commission). This raises governance concerns around a key government rural economic program and could affect public spending credibility.

medium.title: Luhut and National Economic Council Meet President Prabowo at Hambalang Residence
medium.summary: The National Economic Council (DEN), led by Luhut Binsar Pandjaitan and including former ministers Chatib Basri and Mari Elka Pangestu, briefed President Prabowo on the latest national economic developments and strategic recommendations at his private residence in Hambalang. The meeting also covered updates on GovTech digital government transformation aimed at improving data accuracy and social program targeting. This signals active high-level economic policy coordination, which investors should monitor for potential policy shifts.

medium.title: OJK Requests Incentives for Gold ETF and New Financial Products in Meeting with Airlangga
medium.summary: OJK Chairwoman Friderica Widyasari Dewi has formally requested government incentives for new financial sector products, including non-delivery gold Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs), during a meeting with Coordinating Minister Airlangga Hartarto. Gold ETFs allow investors to gain exposure to gold price movements through the stock exchange without physically owning the commodity. If incentives are granted, this could open up a significant new investment product category for Indonesia's growing retail investor base.

medium.title: IDX Expands High Shareholding Concentration List; 37 New Stocks Added, Total Reaches 51 Issuers
medium.summary: Indonesia Stock Exchange (BEI) President Director Jeffrey Hendrik announced the addition of 37 new stocks to the High Shareholding Concentration (HSC) list, bringing the total to 51 issuers, after introducing a new 'price-impact ratio' criterion for stocks with market capitalization above Rp 10 trillion. Stocks on the HSC list are subject to stricter trading rules due to the risk of price manipulation by concentrated ownership. Investors holding or considering these newly listed stocks should be aware of potential trading restrictions that may be applied.

medium.title: JCI Closes Slightly Higher at 6,039 Level
medium.summary: Indonesia's Composite Stock Price Index (IHSG/JCI) closed marginally higher on Tuesday, gaining 1.67 points (0.03%) to settle at 6,039.52, maintaining its position in the 6,000 range. Trading volume reached 37.59 billion shares with a total turnover of Rp 16.82 trillion across 2.81 million transactions. Market breadth was positive with 422 stocks advancing versus 206 declining, indicating cautious but slightly bullish sentiment.
